text:
Consider designing a linear classifier
y = sign(f(x; w, b)),  f(x; w, b) = wᵀx + b
on a dataset D = {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), …, (x_N, y_N)}, xᵢ ∈ ℝᵈ, yᵢ ∈ {+1, −1}, i = 1, 2, …, N. Recall that the sign function outputs +1 if the argument is positive, and −1 if the argument is non-positive. The parameters w and b are updated as per the following training algorithm:
w_new = w_old + yₙxₙ,  b_new = b_old + yₙ
whenever sign(f(xₙ; w_old, b_old)) ≠ yₙ. In other words, whenever the classifier wrongly predicts a sample (xₙ, yₙ) from the dataset, w_old gets updated to w_new, and likewise b_old gets updated to b_new. Consider the case (xₙ, +1), f(xₙ; w_old, b_old) < 0. Then
options: f(xₙ; w_new, b_new) > f(xₙ; w_old, b_old)

f(xₙ; w_new, b_new) = f(xₙ; w_old, b_old)
